headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors: Cline can ingest workspace/MCP content while Firecrawl supplies raw web content and API-driven outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads workspace files, uses MCP, and runs browsers; Firecrawl exposes web scraping/search APIs and MCP-compatible client support. That creates a direct path for attacker-controlled web content or scraped pages to reach Cline as instructions. No provenance tracking or isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is copied into Cline workspace files or MCP inputs, prompt injection is possible.
IF Cline parses scraped web content as instructions without provenance checks, attacker content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Firecrawl outputs into Cline.
Require a human review step before Cline acts on scraped content.
Restrict Cline MCP servers to trusted, allowlisted endpoints.
Strip instructions from scraped text before passing it onward.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/content separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline can read and write workspace files and handles model-provider API keys; Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive code or secrets can flow from Cline into Firecrawl requests or logs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents share the same workspace directory, file contents can be exposed across the pair.
IF either agent forwards its context or files into Firecrawl API calls, secrets may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for Cline and Firecrawl.
Store API keys in distinct secret stores.
Avoid passing full files to Firecrawl unless necessary.
Review outbound requests for secret-bearing fields.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has filesystem write, git modification, shell, and broad network egress; Firecrawl has broad network egress and API-client behavior. They can both mutate shared artifacts if pointed at the same workspace or repo, and Cline explicitly supports multiple instances via filesystem sharing. No locking is documented, so write conflicts are plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git repository or workspace, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF Firecrawl writes generated artifacts into a directory Cline edits, last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize git commits through one operator.
Pause one agent while the other writes.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can act on tool outputs, and Firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data that may be treated as authoritative. If Cline consumes Firecrawl results without verification, errors or poisoned content can cascade into code changes, browser actions, or commits. The downstream blast radius is large because Cline has shell and git authority.
conditions: IF Cline uses Firecrawl output as ground truth without validation, incorrect actions can propagate.
IF Firecrawl returns malformed or adversarial content and Cline commits it, the error becomes persistent.
mitigations: Require source verification before Cline acts on Firecrawl output.
Add a manual approval step for commits and shell actions.
Cross-check scraped facts against a second source.
Limit Firecrawl output to read-only review tasks.
requires-engineering: implement confidence scoring and citation checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys; Firecrawl handles web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys. The profiles do not document residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because both touch screenshots and keys, retention/logging gaps could affect regulated data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through both agents, retention and logging policies must align.
IF one agent stores screenshots or keys longer than the other, compliance mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Document where screenshots and keys are stored.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion controls.
